kbuild.rust_config_prompt: Rust reference driver for Asix PHYs
rust_help: Uses the Rust reference driver for the Asix PHY family (ax88796b_rust.ko).
The intent is to stay within the current safe PHY abstraction subset.

translation.goal: Constrain a strict blind-first `drivers/net/phy/ax88796b_rust.rs` candidate to a minimal, artifact-driven Rust PHY driver covering registration, `read_status`, `suspend`, `resume`, `soft_reset`, and `link_change_notify` for the Asix family without pre-seeding helper-level Rust answers.
translation.abstraction_goal: Keep the driver inside the existing safe PHY abstraction while covering the three Asix variants without driver-side `unsafe`, direct `bindings::*`, reference-driver leakage, or profile-supplied helper recipes.

mvp_scope.note: The strict blind-first acceptance target is build plus lifecycle validation through the fallback oracle until a trusted PHY KUnit runner lands.

behavior_contract: Mirror the C driver's link-update and status-refresh behavior using only the safe PHY abstraction surface.
Preserve the early return when the link remains down.
Recover negotiated link information from safe Clause 22 state instead of driver-side raw register access.
Preserve the generic suspend behavior exposed by the safe PHY device surface instead of open-coding register writes.
Preserve the generic resume behavior exposed by the safe PHY device surface instead of open-coding register writes.
Preserve the Asix reset callback semantics while staying inside the safe PHY reset lifecycle surface.
Only run the reinitialization path when the device transitions through the no-link state.
Keep the notification callback inside the safe PHY device lifecycle surface.

driver_generation_rules: Read only the current experiment artifacts plus the allowlisted generic PHY abstraction files before writing driver code.
Do not read, diff, or quote the upstream Rust reference driver or any archived blind benchmark report before the experiment is frozen.
Use `rust/kernel/net/phy.rs` and `rust/kernel/net/phy/reg.rs` only as the generic safe abstraction surface; keep all module-specific logic constrained by the generated artifact set.

Infer the concrete Rust helper mapping from the C source and the visible safe abstraction signatures; if the mapping is still ambiguous, stop and record a planner/profile gap instead of filling it with driver-side `unsafe`.

private_state.note: The strict blind-first Asix Rust PHY driver should not introduce per-device Rust private state.
